He wants it to spin, slowly and elegantly, like a real diamond turning in the light; to change color with each day, because each day has its own frequency and its own color in the spectrum flow; to radiate light according to the day, because the frequency is light and the jewel is the frequency made visible. "A beautiful frequency of light," he said — "magical," "like a real diamond, like a real jewel or jewelry." That is the Real Object Law applied to the tiniest element on the page, and it is the proof of the law: if the tiniest element has to be a real object, everything does. The 12-second floor on the spin is the same lesson as the orbs — alive is high-tech-computer alive, slow and elegant, never video-game fast.
